axis_note: Classified theory because its load-bearing contribution is Theorem 2, a closed-form bound on the degradation rate. But the paper is two-thirds empirical: three deep-generative modalities (causal transformers, geometric diffusion, VAE) plus a linear-regression theory with numerical confirmation. It touches no layer other than $\Theta$: there is no $W$, no $E$, no retrieval, no test-time state of any kind.
role_in_v2: Part I module T4 (data: augmentation, synthetic and self-generated data, model collapse) and a Part III falsifier. It is the only paper in the corpus that puts a closed form on $\rho$ — the per-round degradation rate — when $\mathcal{R}_k$ in (U-$\Theta$) is generated by the model itself. That is exactly the regime SEAL and Dreaming operate in, so it bounds them from the theory side even though neither line cites it (see cross_path_citations).

problem_stated.headline_question: "The proliferation of generative models, combined with pretraining on web-scale data, raises a timely question: what happens when these models are trained on their own generated outputs?" [Abstract, vendored L20-21]
problem_stated.the_specific_gap_claimed: "those studies largely assumed that new data replace old data over time, where an arguably more realistic assumption is that data accumulate over time. In this paper, we ask: what effect does accumulating data have on model collapse?" [Abstract, L26-27]
problem_stated.why_accumulate_is_the_realistic_assumpti: "subsequent generations of LLMs are often trained with increasing data over time – e.g., 1.4 trillion tokens for Llama 1 (Touvron et al., 2023a), 2 trillion for Llama 2 (Touvron et al., 2023b), 15 trillion for Llama 3 – in which presumably both human-generated and machine-generated data are accumulating in training sets collected from the internet." [§1 Introduction, L137-141]
problem_stated.operational_definition_empirical: "the term model collapse refers to notably worsening error over increasing iterations of the model-data loop, while avoiding model collapse refers instead to bounded error over such iterations." [§2 opening, L176-178]. This is the definition the monograph must hold the paper to — it is a boundedness claim, not a 'gets better' claim.
problem_stated.operational_definition_theoretical: "In this theoretical section, we identify the term model collapse with the situation where test error diverges to infinity (at any rate) as iterations progress." [footnote 3, L564-566]
problem_stated.self_declared_framing: "Our data-accumulating setting is, in some sense, maximally pessimistic: it considers a hypothetical future where synthetic data are uncontrollably dumped on the internet to be vacuumed up for training the next iteration of generative models." [§1, L148-151]
problem_stated.taxonomy_the_paper_itself_insists_on: "'model collapse' – as a term of art – has been used in various ways by various researchers; so care is required in comparing claims across articles. In reviewing the literature, we identified at least four related phenomena: (0) unbounded test error blowup (as here); (1) modal collapse — collapse to one (or a few) modes; (2) collapse to uniformity; and (3) amplification of artifacts introduced by models fit to previous synthetic data." [§4 Discussion, L865-871]. The paper's positive result is about (0) only. It reports evidence that (1) still happens under accumulation in the VAE setting [§2.3, L532-536].

inherited_open_question.finding_for_the_monograph: An un-inherited question is itself the finding here. The model-collapse community in 2024 was arguing with itself about a phenomenon it had named, and nobody in it had posed the accumulation question as an open problem — so this paper had to manufacture its own bridge-in out of a footnote-level remark plus a disagreement over how to read someone else's plot. For the chapter's §N.1 the honest bridge-in is therefore not a quotation from a predecessor but the arithmetic gap the paper points at: prior theory fixed the per-iteration dataset cardinality, and the whole result turns on relaxing that.
inherited_open_question.bridge_in_for_the_chapter: Come in from the Part I T4 module and from the Θ-path chapters: SEAL and Dreaming both build $\mathcal{R}_k$ out of the model's own samples and neither one bounds what repeated rounds do to $\Theta$. This paper is the only place in the corpus where that bound exists — and it exists for a setting neither of them is in.

core_mechanism.one_line: Under (U-$\Theta$) with self-generated $\mathcal{R}_k$, whether $\Theta$ degrades without bound is decided entirely by how $\mathcal{R}_k$ is *composed*: replacing gives a constant per-round penalty and test error linear in $k$, whereas accumulating makes round $i$'s noise enter $\Theta_k$ with weight $1/i$, so its squared-error contribution is $1/i^2$, and the total is bounded by $\pi^2/6$ times the one-round penalty for every $k$.

core_mechanism.reduction_to_frame: Set $W \equiv \varnothing$ and $E \equiv \varnothing$. The paper lives entirely in (U-$\Theta$), and it modifies exactly one thing about it: the composition of $\mathcal{R}_k$. S0's (U-$\Theta$) writes $\mathcal{R}_k = \mathrm{gen}(\mathcal{H}_k;B_s)$ — a fresh per-round set — which is precisely the Replace regime this paper shows to diverge. The Accumulate regime is $\mathcal{R}_k = \mathcal{R}_{k-1}\cup\mathrm{gen}(\mathcal{H}_{k-1};B_s)$ [M-2]. Two further departures from the canonical form matter and must be stated in the chapter's §N.4: (i) the update is $\arg\min$ from a fresh initialisation, not a gradient step from $\Theta_{k-1}$ [M-5], so $\eta_\Theta$ never appears and no forgetting dynamics are modelled; (ii) $\mathrm{gen}$ is unconditional sampling with no filtering, verification, reward, or human review — the paper explicitly lists filtering as future work [§4, L860-861]. The result is therefore a statement about *data mixture schedules*, not about optimisers or about self-improvement.
core_mechanism.the_intuition_in_the_papers_own_words: "in the data accumulation setting, because iteration $i$ contributes fraction $1/i$ to the training dataset, the additional noise from the $i$th iteration of synthetic data has its effect on the model MSE shrunken proportional to $1/i^2$ (due to squared error). The summability of $1/i^2$ prevents the test error from growing indefinitely." [§3.2, L818-822]

outer_vs_inner.readers_first_answer: Nothing in this paper is learned at test time, and nothing moves during a forward pass. There is exactly one learnable object — the model's own weights $\Theta$ — and the only time it moves is when the authors throw the previous model away and train a brand-new one from random initialisation on a corpus of text that the previous model wrote. Everything the paper calls an 'iteration' is a full pretraining run. If you are looking for a wake-time / sleep-time split here, there is none: this is a pure sleep-side paper, and there is no wake side at all.

So measured $\rho$ over rounds 1→4 is roughly +0.19 CE/round under replace and *negative* under accumulate. [Table 2, L1523-1579]
rho.measured_rho_is_temperature_sensitive: Same model at temperature 0.3: replace $t{=}4$ 5.82 (+4.00), $t{=}10$ 9.85 (+8.04) — a factor of ~7 worse at $t{=}4$ than temperature 1.0, from the identical $t{=}1$ baseline of 1.82. Accumulate is essentially unaffected: 1.75 (−0.06). [Table 2, rows 1-2]
rho.measured_rho_other_modalities: Diffusion: 'test loss increases when replacing data ... and test loss remains relatively constant when accumulating data' over 8 rounds — no numbers given, Fig. 4 only [§2.2, L433-436]. VAE: under accumulate 'the test error of accumulating data does increase with the number of iterations (albeit much more slowly than with replacing data)' — i.e. $\rho > 0$ and not shown to be summable; no numbers given, Fig. 5 only [§2.3, L537-538].
rho.the_design_rule_this_yields: A repeated (U-$\Theta$) loop is sustainable iff $\sum_k \rho_k$ converges. Divergence at rate $\log k$ still counts as collapse under the paper's own definition [footnote 3, L564-566].

amortization_A.detail: Equation (A), $C_{\text{avg}} = C_{\text{wake}} + C_{\text{sleep}}/N_q$, presupposes a wake/sleep split over queries sharing a context. This paper has no queries, no contexts, no $N_q$, and no wake cost. It is a training-loop paper end to end.
amortization_A.what_replaces_it: The relevant break-even here is not over queries but over rounds: at what $k$ does retaining $kT$ samples cost more than the error it saves? The paper never poses it, because it never prices either side.

experiments.name: Causal transformer language modelling on TinyStories
experiments.models: GPT-2 at 9M parameters; Llama-2 at 12M, 42M, and 125M parameters per the body text [L188-189]. The figures and Table 2 label the largest model '126M' [Fig. 2 legend L223; Table 2 L1530] and Table 1 labels it '125M' [L367]. The paper is internally inconsistent by 1M on this one model; reproduce both labels rather than picking one.
experiments.data: TinyStories (Eldan & Li, 2023), described by the paper as 'a 470M token GPT-3.5/4-generated dataset of short stories at a kindergarten reading level' [L189].
experiments.token_count: 470M tokens for round 1; each subsequent round samples 'a new dataset of the same size as TinyStories' from the previous round's model [L190-192], so accumulate reaches 470M × $k$ tokens at round $k$.
experiments.training_protocol: one epoch per round [L189]; 'a newly initialized model' is pretrained each round on the replaced or concatenated dataset [L193-194].
experiments.rounds: 5 model-fitting iterations in Figs. 2 and 3 (x-axis 1-5); 10 for the replace regime at GPT-2 9M and its small-dataset variant only [Table 2, 't=10 (repl)' column].
experiments.generation: sampling temperature 1.0 (default) and 0.3 (ablation) [L194-195]. Dataset generation implemented with vllm (Kwon et al., 2023); training with Huggingface Transformers (Wolf et al., 2019) [App. C, L1492-1494].
experiments.metric: cross-entropy validation/test loss. No downstream benchmark, no accuracy, no perplexity-on-external-corpus, no human eval — loss and hand-picked samples only.
experiments.column_legend: '(*) indicates a replacement regime with growing dataset size to ablate for total train set size' [Table 2 caption, L1577-1579] — i.e. the empirical Replace-Multiple control.
experiments.precision_note: Three of the reported deltas do not equal the difference of the two displayed values: GPT-2 9M accumulate 1.82→1.74 is printed as (−0.07) not (−0.08); GPT-2 9M replace 1.82→2.39 as (+0.58) not (+0.57); Llama-2 126M replace 1.71→2.23 as (+0.53) not (+0.52); temp=0.3 replace 1.82→9.85 as (+8.04) not (+8.03). Consistent with the deltas being computed from unrounded values. Reproduce the table as printed and do not silently 'fix' it.
experiments.qualitative_result: Table 1 [L366-409] shows generations for Llama2 (125M) at iterations 3(A), 3(R), 8(R) and GPT2 (9M) at 5(A), 5(R), 10(R). The replace samples degrade into non-sequiturs ('Mamaing Grandma's possibilitant, twice would measure how much she lovedk'); the accumulate samples remain coherent.
experiments.stated_findings: 'for all architectures, parameter counts, and sampling temperatures, as the number of model-fitting iterations increased, replacing data led to an increase in test cross entropy' and 'accumulating data led to equal-or-lower test cross entropy' [L355-359]. 'Lower temperature (0.3) led to a faster increase in test error than higher temperature (1.0)' [L359-360].
ablations: Dataset-size control ('replace-multiple'): fully synthetic corpus grown to match the accumulated size. 'We find that model performance still degrades (albeit at a lower rate)' [L411-415; Table 2 column '(*)'].
Iteration-1 model quality: training amount in the first round varied over 0.25 / 0.5 / 1.0 epochs; 'no significant impact' / 'no qualitative differences' [L416-419; Fig. 14, L2038-2040].
Dataset size and epochs: 1/5 of TinyStories at 1 and 3 epochs; 'no qualitative effect' [L1514-1517; Table 2 rows 3-4].

experiments.name: Geometric diffusion on molecular conformations
experiments.model: GeoDiff (Xu et al., 2022), a geometric diffusion model for molecular conformation generation. Parameter count not reported.
experiments.data: GEOM-Drugs (Axelrod & Gomez-Bombarelli, 2022), training split down-sampled to 40,000 molecular conformations as the initial training set [L428-429].
experiments.protocol: 50 diffusion steps per prediction [L429-430]; loss = GeoDiff's standard weighted variational lower bound to the conditional likelihood [L430-432]; 8 model-fitting iterations.
experiments.result: 'test loss increases when replacing data, matching our language model experiments, and test loss remains relatively constant when accumulating data (Fig. 4)' [L433-434].
experiments.shape_of_the_replace_curve: 'Unlike with language models, we found that when replacing data, performance worsens significantly in the first model-fitting iteration trained on synthetic data and does not degrade further substantially in subsequent iterations.' [L434-436]
experiments.numbers: none. The paper reports no numeric loss values for this experiment; Fig. 4's axis spans roughly 100 to 300 with no tick values quoted in text. Any number the chapter wants must come from reading the figure, which the monograph should not do.

experiments.name: Variational autoencoders on CelebA
experiments.model: convolutional VAE: 5 conv layers with 32, 64, 128, 256, 512 channels and a mirrored conv decoder; 128-dimensional isotropic Gaussian latent represented by 2 MLP layers [App. D, L2049-2051]. Parameter count not reported.
experiments.data: CelebA (Liu et al., 2015), '200k images of human faces split between train and test sets' [L513-515]; cropped and down-sampled to 64×64 pixels [L2048-2049].
experiments.protocol: 'Each data iteration consists of 100 training epochs, after which we generate 163K new training images by sampling latents from the Gaussian prior and then passing them through the generator model' [L2052-2054]. Loss = reconstruction error + KL to the isotropic Gaussian prior [L517-519]. 8+ model-fitting iterations (Fig. 5 x-axis 0-8). Baseline for comparison = 100 training epochs on the real dataset [Fig. 6 right, L528-529].
experiments.result_replace: 'the test error rises swiftly with each additional iteration, and each iteration yields lower quality and less diverse generated faces until all model generations represent a single mode' [L520-522].
experiments.result_accumulate: 'accumulating data at each iteration significantly slows model collapse: the test error increases significantly slower with each additional iteration' [L531-532]. And explicitly: 'unlike language modeling, the test error of accumulating data does increase with the number of iterations (albeit much more slowly than with replacing data)' [L537-538].
experiments.diversity_result: 'While the diversity of generations does go down as compared in the middle and right panel of Fig. 6, it still represents major axes of variation in the dataset, such as gender, but no longer seems to generate other details, along more minor axis of the data manifold, such as glasses and accessories.' [L532-536]
experiments.reconstruction_vs_sampling_split: App. D reports the opposite for reconstructions: the accumulate model 'still maintains it's capabilities and generates accurate reconstructions, including smaller details such as glasses and hats', with the authors hypothesising that these details survive as a minor sub-manifold that prior samples rarely hit [L2059-2064]. So under accumulation the *encoder-decoder capability* survives while the *sampled distribution's tails* do not.
experiments.numbers: none. Fig. 5's axis spans roughly 0.020 to 0.030 test loss with no values quoted in text.
experiments.contradicting_external_evidence_the_pape: 'we also note that Martínez et al. (2023a) found slightly contradictory evidence, specifically that a different architecture on a much smaller dataset exhibits fast performance deterioration even with accumulating data. Understanding under what conditions and why these discrepancies exist is an interesting direction we leave for future research.' [L538-542]

experiments.name: Linear-regression numerics, main text
experiments.setup: ridge regularisation 0; data dimension $d_{\text{in}} = 32$; samples per iteration $T \in \{100, 316, 1000\}$; noise $\sigma^2 \in \{0.01, 0.1, 1.0, 10.0, 100.0\}$; 10 model-fitting iterations; both numerical and theoretical curves overlaid [Fig. 7 headers and legend, L639-666].
experiments.result: 'The numerics almost perfectly matched the analytics (Fig. 7): when data are replaced, the test error grows with the number of iterations $n$, with the prefactor set by the noise-to-signal ratio $\sigma^2 d/(T-d-1)$, but when data accumulate, the test error rapidly plateaus with the prefactor similarly set.' [L828-831]
experiments.numbers: no tabulated values; agreement is asserted from the overlaid curves.

experiments.name: Linear-regression numerics, extended — the three-regime comparison
experiments.setup: ridge regularisation 0.0; data dimension $d_{\text{in}} = 10$; $T \in \{100, 316, 1000\}$; $\sigma^2 \in \{0.1, 1.0, 10.0\}$; up to 200 model-fitting iterations; log-scaled test squared error; three rows — Replace, Replace-Multiple, Accumulate.
experiments.result: Replace grows linearly, Replace-Multiple grows logarithmically, Accumulate has a finite upper bound independent of the number of iterations [Fig. 16 caption, L2235-2247].
experiments.why_this_is_the_figure_that_matters: It is the only place in the paper where the compute/data-matched control is shown over a long horizon. At 200 iterations the logarithmic divergence of Replace-Multiple is visible; at the 5-10 iterations of the language-model experiments it would not be.

experiments.name: Re-analysis of prior work's figure (not a new experiment)
experiments.content: Fig. 8 reproduces Figure 7 of Alemohammad et al. (2023) — StyleGAN2 on FlickrFaces 128×128 — and argues that their 'synthetic augmentation loop' curve plateaus rather than diverging, against those authors' own stated conclusion that fixed real data 'only delays the inevitable degradation'.
experiments.status: This is an argument about someone else's plot, not a replication. The monograph must present it as such.

scale_ceiling.largest_model: 125M–126M parameter Llama-2 (label inconsistent between body text and tables) [§2.1 L188-189; Table 2 L1530]. Every other model is ≤42M.
scale_ceiling.largest_token_count: 470M tokens of real data at round 1; the accumulate corpus reaches 470M × 5 ≈ 2.35B tokens at round 5 [§2.1 L189-192]. [book arithmetic from L189-192, one epoch per round] processing the full 5-round accumulate sweep costs 470M × (1+2+3+4+5) = 7.05B training tokens against 470M × 5 = 2.35B for replace, plus 470M × 4 = 1.88B tokens of generation in either case. The paper states none of these three totals.
scale_ceiling.longest_loop: 5 model-fitting iterations for accumulate; 10 for replace, and only for GPT-2 9M and its small-dataset variant [Table 2]. 8 iterations for diffusion and VAE. 200 iterations for the linear model — the only long horizon in the paper is the toy one.
scale_ceiling.modalities: three (text, molecular conformation, images) plus a linear toy. Breadth is the paper's real empirical strength; depth is not.
scale_ceiling.benchmarks: none. There is no downstream task evaluation anywhere: no accuracy, no QA, no reasoning benchmark, no human evaluation. All claims rest on held-out loss plus six hand-picked text samples in Table 1.
scale_ceiling.seeds_and_variance: none reported. 'seed', 'error bar', 'std', 'confidence' all return zero hits in the vendored text. Every curve in Figs. 2-5 and every entry in Table 2 is a single run.
scale_ceiling.gap_to_the_phenomenon_it_motivates: The introduction motivates the work with Llama 1/2/3 at 1.4T / 2T / 15T tokens [§1, L137-140]. The validation is at 470M tokens and ≤126M parameters — roughly 3 to 4.5 orders of magnitude below in tokens and 3+ orders below in parameters, on a corpus of kindergarten-level short stories that was itself written by GPT-3.5/4.
scale_ceiling.summary: The empirical ceiling is 126M parameters × 470M tokens × 5 self-training rounds on one narrow synthetic corpus, with no seeds and no benchmark. The theoretical ceiling is an underparameterised, well-specified, ridgeless, isotropic linear regression with frozen covariates. Everything between those two ceilings — a real pretraining-scale model on web-distributed data with an incrementally updated checkpoint — is untested.

new.definition: three schedules for composing $\mathcal{R}_k$ in a self-training loop: keep everything and append; discard and regenerate at fixed size; discard and regenerate at growing size $kT$.
new.why_the_monograph_needs_it: It is the taxonomy that makes 'the model trains on its own output' a question with more than one answer. Owned by the T4 module.

new.definition: (0) unbounded test-error blow-up; (1) modal collapse to one or a few modes; (2) collapse to uniformity; (3) amplification of artefacts introduced by models fit to previous synthetic data.
new.why_the_monograph_needs_it: The paper refutes (0) and simultaneously exhibits (1) in its own VAE samples. Any chapter that says 'accumulation avoids collapse' without naming the sense is wrong by the paper's own standard.

new.concept: summability of $\rho$ as the stability criterion
new.definition: a repeated (U-$\Theta$) loop is sustainable iff $\sum_k \rho_k < \infty$; the $1/i$ weighting of round-$i$ noise in the parameters becomes $1/i^2$ in squared error, and $\sum 1/i^2$ converges while $\sum 1/i$ does not.
new.why_the_monograph_needs_it: It converts the frame's $\rho$ cell from a reported measurement into a design criterion.

new.concept: $\pi^2/6$ as the price of infinite self-training
new.definition: $\mathcal{L}^{\text{acc}}_{\text{test}} \le (\pi^2/6)\cdot\sigma^2 d_{\text{in}}/(T-d_{\text{in}}-1) \approx 1.645\times$ the single-round penalty, for all $k$.
new.why_the_monograph_needs_it: a memorable, falsifiable constant to hang the T4 module on.

extended_or_renamed.change: S0 defines $\mathcal{R}_k = \mathrm{gen}(\mathcal{H}_k;B_s)$, silently a per-round set. This paper shows the union-vs-replacement choice is the difference between divergence and a constant bound, so the frame must make the schedule explicit: $\mathcal{R}_k = \mathcal{R}_{k-1}\cup\mathrm{gen}(\mathcal{H}_{k-1};B_s)$ is a *different rule*, not a detail.
extended_or_renamed.action_for_S0: record the accumulation schedule as a first-class parameter of (U-$\Theta$), alongside $\eta_\Theta$.

extended_or_renamed.change: the frame defines $\rho$ as 'performance loss per round'. This paper shows the meaningful object is the *sequence* $\{\rho_k\}$ and its partial sums, not a scalar. A constant $\rho$ and a $1/k^2$ $\rho$ are qualitatively different systems.
extended_or_renamed.action_for_S0: state $\rho$ as a sequence with a convergence test.

extended_or_renamed.change: this paper instantiates $\mathrm{gen}$ as unconditional, unfiltered sampling at a fixed temperature. SEAL and Dreaming instantiate it with task conditioning and (in SEAL's case) reward-based selection. The frame should distinguish filtered from unfiltered $\mathrm{gen}$, because this paper's bound is proved only for the unfiltered case.

for the $\Theta$-path the frame assumes the persistent state is a weight delta. Under Accumulate the persistent state is the *retained corpus*, which grows linearly in $k$ while $\Theta$ stays fixed-size. The $\Theta$-path has a data tail as well as a weight tail.
extended_or_renamed.action_for_S0: split $C_{\text{cap}}$ into weight-state and retained-data-state for $\Theta$-path chapters.

retired.concept: 'the curse of recursion' as an unconditional law
retired.reason: 'these results strongly suggest that the "curse of recursion" may not be as dire as had been portrayed – provided we accumulate synthetic data alongside real data, rather than replacing real data by synthetic data only.' [§4, L854-856]. The conditional clause is the whole content and must never be dropped when the claim is cited.

retired.concept: 'accumulation merely delays collapse' (Alemohammad et al.'s reading of their own experiment)
retired.reason: disputed by this paper's re-reading of their Fig. 7 [App. A L1078-1084, Fig. 8]. Retired only as a *contested* claim — the dispute is not settled by new evidence, and Martínez et al. (2023a) still stands against the accumulate result [L538-541].

open_questions.q: What happens when *additional real data* is introduced at each model-fitting iteration, rather than only at round 1?
open_questions.quote: "in future work we would like to explore different data generation and accumulation regimes, such as (1) additional 'real' data being introduced in each model-fitting iteration"
open_questions.bridge_out: This is the regime every deployed system is actually in. Nobody in the corpus answers it.

open_questions.q: What do different schedules of synthetic-data volume per iteration do?
open_questions.quote: "(2) different schedules of how much synthetic data is generated at each iteration"
open_questions.bridge_out: Directly the $B_s$ axis of the monograph. The paper's own Replace-Multiple result [Eq. 11] shows the schedule alone can change the divergence rate from linear to logarithmic, so this is not a minor sweep.

open_questions.q: What does human filtering of generated data do — e.g. RLHF-style selection?
open_questions.quote: "(3) human-filtering of generated data, e.g., as done in RLHF"
open_questions.bridge_out: This is exactly SEAL's regime (reward-selected self-edits). The bound in this paper is proved for the *unfiltered* case only, so it neither licenses nor forbids SEAL's loop.

open_questions.q: What happens under deterministic generation — greedy decoding, temperature 0?
open_questions.quote: "we note that in all our experiments, the synthetic dataset is generated by sampling from the previous model, i.e., with some stochasticity; in future work, we would like to explore also what happens if data is generated deterministically, e.g. with temperature 0 in a typical language model."
open_questions.bridge_out: The production default is low-temperature or greedy decoding, and the paper's own temperature ablation shows the *lower* temperature is far worse under replace (9.85 vs 2.91 CE at $t{=}10$) [Table 2]. The untested direction is the one that matters.

open_questions.q: Which of the four distinct 'model collapse' phenomena occurs under which conditions, and which countermeasure addresses each?
open_questions.quote: "Future work should map out what factors cause which to occur and what preventative strategies are effective at addressing each."
open_questions.bridge_out: The paper's own VAE result is a live instance: phenomenon (0) is avoided while phenomenon (1) is not.

open_questions.q: Why does accumulation fail to bound error for some architectures and datasets (Martínez et al. 2023a; the paper's own VAEs)?
open_questions.quote: "Understanding under what conditions and why these discrepancies exist is an interesting direction we leave for future research."
open_questions.bridge_out: This is the falsification hook for Part III: the accumulate result is modality-dependent and the paper says so.

open_questions.q: What are the right baselines beyond Replace-Multiple?
open_questions.quote: "Other baselines are also possible, but we leave these to future work."

open_questions.q: Is there an optimal strategy for avoiding collapse?
open_questions.quote: "To our knowledge, no paper has claimed an 'optimal' strategy to avoid model collapse, and neither has ours."
open_questions.bridge_out: Explicitly disclaims optimality. Accumulate is shown to be *sufficient* in the linear model, never necessary and never best.

open_questions.q: Does the bound survive ridge regularisation and kernel methods?
open_questions.quote: "although we present our results in the context of ordinary linear regression in $\mathbb{R}^d$, our analysis can be readily extended to ridge regression and the kernel setting"
open_questions.bridge_out: Asserted, not shown. Every reported numeric pins ridge to 0 [Fig. 7 L639; Fig. 16 L2153]. Dohmatob et al. (2024a) is credited with results on *optimal regularisation* as a collapse mitigation [App. A, L1024-1027]; this paper does not engage that lever.

open_questions.q: [note-writer, not stated by the paper] Does the bound survive when $\Theta_k$ is updated incrementally from $\Theta_{k-1}$ instead of retrained from scratch?
open_questions.source: implied by §2.1 L193-194 and §3.1 L625, both of which retrain from a fresh solve/init
open_questions.bridge_out: This is the single most important unasked question for the $\Theta$-path chapters, because SEAL, Dreaming and SCM all update a live checkpoint. The paper's mechanism — 1/i weighting of round-i noise because round-i data is 1/i of the corpus — has no obvious analogue when the previous parameters, not the previous data, are the carrier.

unfavorable_facts.fact: In one of the paper's three deep-generative modalities, the headline result does not hold. For VAEs on CelebA the paper states plainly that accumulation only *slows* the growth: 'unlike language modeling, the test error of accumulating data does increase with the number of iterations (albeit much more slowly than with replacing data)'.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_matters: By the paper's own definition — 'avoiding model collapse refers instead to bounded error over such iterations' [§2, L176-178] — the VAE experiment does not show collapse being avoided. Yet the figure caption reads 'Data Accumulation Avoids Model Collapse in Variational Autoencoders for Image Generation' [Fig. 5, L505-508] and the section is titled to match. The abstract's 'We obtain similar results for deep generative models on other types of real data' [L32-33] overstates this one.
unfavorable_facts.category: ablation that reverses / caption overclaims the measurement

unfavorable_facts.fact: Under accumulation the VAE's generative diversity still degrades: 'the diversity of generations does go down ... it still represents major axes of variation in the dataset, such as gender, but no longer seems to generate other details, along more minor axis of the data manifold, such as glasses and accessories.'
unfavorable_facts.why_it_matters: Bounded loss does not mean a preserved distribution. Tail loss is precisely the failure mode Dohmatob et al. (2024b) analyse and the mechanism most relevant to a knowledge-consolidation system. App. D adds that reconstructions *do* retain glasses and hats [L2059-2064] — so the encoder survives while the sampled distribution's tails do not, which is a subtler and worse story for anyone whose sleep loop re-samples its own outputs.
unfavorable_facts.category: surviving failure mode under the winning configuration

unfavorable_facts.fact: The 'real data' anchoring the flagship language-model experiment is itself model-generated. TinyStories is described by the paper as 'a 470M token GPT-3.5/4-generated dataset of short stories at a kindergarten reading level'.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_matters: The whole result is about mixing real with synthetic. Round 1's 'real' corpus is GPT-3.5/4 output, and the distribution being protected is kindergarten-level English with very low entropy and short-range structure. Whether the 1/i² argument survives a heavy-tailed web distribution is untested, and Dohmatob et al. (2024b) — cited here — is specifically about what tails do.
unfavorable_facts.category: the control condition is not what it is called

unfavorable_facts.fact: The compute- and data-matched control still degrades. In the linear theory, Replace-Multiple diverges logarithmically [Eq. 11, App. E L2126-2141]. Empirically, the size-matched replace regime still gets worse: GPT-2 (9M) reaches 2.18 (+0.36) at $t{=}4$ versus 1.82 at $t{=}1$, compared with 2.39 (+0.58) for plain replace.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_matters: It establishes that 'more data' is not the mechanism — but it also means the paper's own honest baseline never reaches boundedness, so the claim rests entirely on retaining real data forever, an operational requirement the paper never prices.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The accumulate curves *improve* relative to round 1 (e.g. 1.82 → 1.74 for GPT-2 9M; 1.71 → 1.59 for Llama-2 126M at $t{=}4$), and the paper itself notes the comparison is not step-matched: 'Epochs correspond to more gradient steps for accumulate than replace because the number of training data grows for accumulate.'
unfavorable_facts.source: Table 2, L1523-1579; Fig. 3 caption note, L345-347
unfavorable_facts.why_it_matters: Part of the accumulate advantage in the deep-model experiments is simply a larger corpus and more optimisation, at higher cost. Nothing in Table 2 is compute-matched, and no compute figure is given that would let a reader normalise.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The theory freezes the covariates. The 'accumulated' design matrix is $k$ stacked copies of the *same* $X$: $\tilde X_n^{\top} = [\tilde X_{n-1}^{\top}; X^{\top}]$, and only the targets $\hat Y$ are ever regenerated.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_matters: The theorem bounds accumulated *label* noise. It says nothing about drift of the input distribution, which is exactly what happens when a language model generates its own next training corpus. The empirical loops do regenerate inputs, and the modality where inputs matter most (images) is the one where the bound fails.

unfavorable_facts.fact: Every assumption of Theorem 2 removes a known source of collapse: underparameterised ($T \ge d_{\text{in}}$, $X$ full column rank), well-specified (the true $\Theta^{*}$ lies in the fitted class), ridgeless, isotropic ($\Sigma = I_{d_{\text{in}}}$), $T \ge d_{\text{in}}+2$, i.i.d. Gaussian noise of *constant* variance $\sigma^2$ at every round.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_matters: There is no bias term anywhere in the analysis — test error is defined as $\mathbb{E}\lVert\Theta-\Theta^{*}\rVert^2_\Sigma$ [Eq. 1, L716-727], pure variance. So the theorem proves that *re-injected label-noise variance is summable under accumulation*, which is true and clean but is a strictly weaker statement than 'model collapse does not occur'. Approximation error, tail truncation, mode loss, and over-parameterisation are all assumed away.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The update rule studied is a from-scratch retrain, not an incremental weight update. 'In each model-fitting iteration, we then pretrain a newly initialized model'; in the theory, $\Theta_k = \tilde X_k^{\dagger}\tilde Y_k$, a fresh closed-form solve.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_matters: $\eta_\Theta$ never appears; no optimiser state, no checkpoint continuity, no catastrophic forgetting is modelled. Nothing here bounds a system that edits a live $\Theta$ round after round — which is what SEAL, Dreaming and SCM do. Using this paper as a guarantee for those systems is unlicensed.

unfavorable_facts.fact: Generation is unconditional, unfiltered, unverified sampling. No reward, no selection, no deduplication, no human review anywhere in the loop; filtering is listed as future work.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_matters: Cuts both ways and the chapter must say both: it makes the setting genuinely pessimistic, and it makes the result inapplicable to any pipeline that filters — which is every deployed self-improvement pipeline.

unfavorable_facts.fact: External evidence against the result is acknowledged and left unresolved: 'Martínez et al. (2023a) found slightly contradictory evidence, specifically that a different architecture on a much smaller dataset exhibits fast performance deterioration even with accumulating data.'
unfavorable_facts.why_it_matters: The generality claim ('these results hold across a range of model sizes, architectures, and hyperparameters', Abstract L31-32) has a named counterexample in the literature that this paper does not reproduce, refute, or explain.

unfavorable_facts.fact: One of the paper's supporting data points is a re-reading of someone else's figure against those authors' own conclusion, not a new experiment. Fig. 8 reproduces Alemohammad et al.'s Fig. 7 and argues 'we believe that a closer examination of their results (App. Fig. 8) reveals that accumulating data causes the test error to plateau'.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_matters: It is an interpretive dispute over a plot in a paper the authors did not run. The monograph should cite it as a disagreement, not as evidence.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The diffusion result's shape contradicts the theory's replace prediction. 'when replacing data, performance worsens significantly in the first model-fitting iteration trained on synthetic data and does not degrade further substantially in subsequent iterations.'
unfavorable_facts.why_it_matters: Eq. (4) predicts error growing *linearly in $k$* under replace. The diffusion experiment shows a one-step drop and then a plateau. That is a real mismatch between the paper's theory and one of its own three modalities, and the paper does not comment on it.

unfavorable_facts.fact: No seeds, no repeats, no error bars, no confidence intervals anywhere. Search of the vendored text for 'seed', 'error bar', 'std', 'confidence' returns zero hits.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_matters: The accumulate-vs-baseline gaps in Table 2 are 0.06-0.28 cross-entropy on single runs. The replace-vs-accumulate gaps are large enough to survive most plausible run-to-run variance; the accumulate-*improves* claim is not.

unfavorable_facts.fact: No downstream benchmark of any kind. Every quantitative claim is held-out loss; the only qualitative evidence is six hand-picked generations in Table 1.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_matters: The monograph's cost frame asks what the sleep round buys. This paper can only answer in nats, never in task performance.

systems_implications.decode_cost: Unchanged, by construction. The artefact of a sleep round is a retrained $\Theta$ with identical architecture and identical parameter count [§2.1, L188-194]; there is no added state at inference, no KV-cache change, no retrieval hop, no per-token overhead. This is the $\Theta$-path's structural advantage over the E-path and it costs nothing at decode — which is exactly why its cost has to be looked for somewhere else.
systems_implications.batching: [note-writer inference, grounded in §2.1 L190-194] Shared-weight batching survives here. The Rosetta row 'batch로 weight 공유 → Θ-경로에서 깨짐' applies to *per-user* weight deltas; this paper's loop produces one global $\Theta$ per round for the whole population. The monograph must therefore distinguish population-level $\Theta$-path (this paper, and pretraining-scale self-training generally) from per-user $\Theta$-path (SEAL-style per-context self-edits). Only the second breaks batching.
systems_implications.where_the_sleep_traffic_lands: Two workloads with opposite profiles, both grounded in §2.1 L189-194. (a) Generation: producing a full 470M-token corpus per round by sampling from $\Theta_{k-1}$ is a pure batch-decode job — memory-bandwidth-bound, weights resident in HBM, output streamed to storage. The paper used vLLM for it [App. C, L1494], which is the one place the reader's own world touches this paper. (b) Training: a compute-bound pass over a corpus that grows linearly in $k$, read sequentially from cold storage. Nothing in this loop is latency-sensitive and nothing lands in a cache hierarchy in an interesting way; the pressure is on storage capacity and sequential read bandwidth.
systems_implications.bytes_and_capacity: [book arithmetic from L189-192, L2048-2053; the paper reports no bytes] Text: 470M tokens per round at 2 bytes/token as uint16 ids ≈ 0.94 GB per round, so the accumulate corpus is ≈ 4.7 GB at round 5 and grows without bound in $k$. Images: 163K generated images per VAE iteration at 64×64×3 uint8 = 12,288 B each ≈ 2.0 GB per iteration. These are small absolutely, but the *shape* is the point: under Accumulate the persistent state of a $\Theta$-path system is not the weight delta — it is the retained corpus, and it is $\Theta(k)$ while $\Theta$ itself is $\Theta(1)$.
systems_implications.the_cost_the_paper_recommends_and_never_: [book arithmetic from L189-192 and App. E L2143-2144] Per round, generation costs $T$ samples (constant) while training costs $|\mathcal{R}_k| = kT$ samples. Over $K$ rounds that is $\Theta(K^2 T)$ training tokens against $\Theta(KT)$ for replace. Concretely for the paper's own 5-round sweep: 7.05B training tokens for accumulate versus 2.35B for replace, from an identical 1.88B tokens of generation. The paper states the asymmetry in words twice [Fig. 3 note L345-347; App. E L2143-2144] and never as a number.
systems_implications.capacity_scaling: $C_{\text{cap}}$ for this mechanism splits in two: weight state, flat at the model's own size and unchanged by the loop; and data state, linear in the number of rounds and never discarded. S0's $C_{\text{cap}}$ cell assumes the first. This paper is the reason the $\Theta$-path chapters need both.
systems_implications.failure_mode_a_systems_reader_should_wat: Aggregate loss can stay bounded while the sampled distribution loses its tails — the VAE result [§2.3, L532-536], where test loss grows slowly but glasses and accessories stop being generated. A production monitor watching held-out perplexity would not fire. If a sleep loop's output feeds the next round's input, tail loss is self-amplifying even when the loss curve looks flat.
systems_implications.the_one_number_a_serving_engineer_can_ta: $\pi^2/6 \approx 1.6449$. If your self-training loop retains all prior data including the original real corpus, and your setting matches the theorem's assumptions, the total lifetime degradation of running it forever is bounded by 1.645 times what one round costs you [model-collapse Eq. 3]. If instead you discard, you pay that once per round, forever [Eq. 4]. If you keep only synthetic but grow it, you pay $\log k$ [Eq. 11].
systems_implications.what_this_paper_does_not_let_you_conclud: Nothing about latency, nothing about serving, nothing about per-user state, nothing about an incrementally updated checkpoint, and nothing about a filtered or verified generation pipeline. Every one of those is out of scope by construction, not merely unmeasured.
